content:
sam: kicking off ORD network on‑ramp provisioning. need quick eyes on transit attachment + nat egress plan. going to try blue/green TGW attachments so we can failover cleanly.
priya: @sam quick Q — are we using a separate DNS zone for ORD or delegating into redwood-infra.global?
sam: delegating subzone ord.redwood-infra.global to route53 in acct-ord. I'll add NS + IAM for operations.
jules: for TGW: prefer explicit route priorities: keep ORD in a separate route table and only advertise to prod when health checks pass. that reduces blast radius.
ben: +1. also we should lock down egress to corporate proxy for initial rollout. will push an egress ACL that denies 0.0.0.0/0 and allows proxy CIDR.
sam: plan: 1) create VPCs (gpu-pool, infra-control, bastion) 2) attach to TGW as spoke attachments 3) create route tables and propagate on green only 4) NAT policy + egress ACL to proxy 5) delegate DNS ord subzone 6) smoke tests + handoff doc.
priya: do we have the TGW attachment tags that the automation expects? last time missing tag blocked terraform apply. tag key = redwood:env, value = ord-prod or ord-canary
sam: yep will tag as ord-canary for green, ord-prod for blue once we flip.
infra-bot: terraform apply started for network/ord/vpcs — plan: 12 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
ben: workaround note: if aws refuses tgw association due to pending delete in another acct, ping netops@ and include attachment id. happened last week.
jules: healthchecks: create a lambda that hits a small http endpoint behind ALB in infra-control, returns 200 within 250ms. TGW routes to be enabled only when lambda passes 3 consecutive checks.
priya: DNS checks after delegation: run from an external host `dig +trace ord.redwood-infra.global` and confirm NS set to route53. also check internal resolver via `dig @10.0.0.2 service.internal.ord.redwood-infra.global`.
sam: putting quick smoke test checklist here: 
```
# smoke.sh
set -e
# 1. TGW route lookup
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=ord-spoke-rt
# 2. outbound internet test via proxy
curl -sS -H "Host: example.com" --proxy http://proxy.ord.corp:3128 http://example.com/health
# 3. dns internal
dig @10.0.0.2 api.internal.ord.redwood-infra.global +short
```

ben: also verify kernel params on gpu instances: `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward` should be 1 for NAT hosts. and `conntrack` table size — bump to 524288 for heavy throughput.
priya: cost note: enabling TGW data transfer alerted finance last time. Estimated cross-AZ traffic in ORD could be ~$0.03/GB. flagging to infra-costs so they can estimate for reserved capacity.
sam: good call, assigning financial runbook item.
infra-bot: smoke.sh returned: step1 ok, step2 proxy timeout, step3 returned 10.10.5.12
ben: proxy timeout — likely egress ACL blocking. I'm applying allow for proxy CIDR 10.50.0.0/24 on ord-spoke-nat-sg.
priya: after that I'll re-run `dig` from internal host and confirm recursion works and TLS certs are in the vault for ALB.
jules: also schedule a controlled canary for a low-priority GPU workload: run 3 models for 2h with reduced batch size. observe latency + conntrack metrics.
sam: timeline: today = infra creation + TGW attach canary; tomorrow = DNS delegation + egress policy; day after = canary workload + handoff.
ben: once canary is green I'll add a temporary fallback route to a secondary region (IAD) with lower preference. will document route priority.
priya: handoff checklist for support on call: pager duty escalation, playbook link, short command snippets to rollback (route table propagation disable command), and contacts.
sam: putting contacts: @priya (network), @ben (runtime), @jules (validation). will create PR for runbook in docs repo.
infra-bot: deploy succeeded: aws-autoscale-gpu-subnet applied.
ben: re-run smoke.sh: step1 ok, step2 proxy ok, step3 returns expected A record. :thumbsup:
sam: excellent. leaving this thread open for final canary results. tagging support for Friday handoff. :white_check_mark:
priya: FYI I added a note in the dns-delegation doc about TTLs — set initial TTL to 60s during rollout.
jules: canary started 12:10 UTC, baseline latency 120ms -> current 150ms, no conntrack exhaustion. monitoring for 2h.
ben: if we see >20% latency increase we'll fallback route and pause batch size.
priya: handoff doc PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/infrastructure/runbooks/pulls/42 — ready for review.
sam: thanks everyone. I'll update the runbook with the TGW route table ids and attach the smoke logs.
infra-bot: thread archived after 78s of inactivity.
